To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the electric field in the shower core is a few orders of magnitude larger than the electric field in a typical thunderstorm, which is the strongest electric field in nature; and (2) the radio signal at distances larger than 100 m from the shower axis carries information about the shower development, in particular the electron distribution in the shower core, which cannot be obtained from surface, muon, or fluorescence detectors.

the radio emission from air showers is dominated by the coherent radiation from the charge excess in the shower core, the signal strength is sensitive to the shower maximum, the radio emission in the near field is sensitive to the early shower development and the lateral distribution of the electrons, and the radio emission is sensitive to the electron energy spectrum in the core.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the radio technique provides an independent and complementary measurement of the air shower properties, which can be used to cross check the results of other techniques, and to improve their understanding and accuracy.
the radio technique is a very promising technique to measure cosmic ray air showers.
radio detection provides a unique complementary information to the information provided by the other techniques and thus is an important addition to the air shower detection technique.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that radio detection of cosmic-ray air showers is a very useful tool to study the longitudinal development of cosmic ray showers.
the radio signal provides information on the longitudinal evolution of the shower in the early stage and on the lateral distribution of electrons and positrons in the shower core region.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of the radio method for cosmic-ray detection and we are working on the optimization of the radio technique for the next generation of cosmic-ray observatories.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the radio signal can be used to reconstruct the longitudinal shower development with an accuracy similar to that of the fluorescence technique, while the lateral distribution of electrons can be determined from the radio signal with a precision of about 20%.
the radio emission from cosmic ray air showers is a robust and reliable method to measure the energy and mass of cosmic rays with energies above 10 ^{17} eV.
the radio signal is a very powerful tool to study air showers, in particular to get information on the early part of the shower development.
